prose: Nilay Patel interviews Benn Jordan - musician, YouTuber and researcher - who has become the most visible investigator of Flock Safety, the automatic license plate reader company, and recently testified before the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism at a hearing dedicated to Flock and other ALPR systems.

The backlash he helped build is bipartisan and now resembles the pushback against AI data centers: hundreds of cities, counties and local governments have canceled Flock contracts, Republican Sen. Josh Hawley has opened an investigation, and Reuters reported Flock plans to cut about 18 percent of its workforce. The conversation digs into how a creator ended up as the face of the anti-Flock movement and where the surveillance fight goes next.
highlights: Decoder interview with Benn Jordan on Flock Safety and ALPR surveillance
Jordan testified at a Senate Judiciary subcommittee hearing on ALPR systems
Hundreds of local governments have canceled Flock contracts
Sen. Josh Hawley investigating Flock; ~18% workforce cut reported
Backlash is bipartisan and compared to AI data center pushback
Jordan pairs a music career with creator-led surveillance investigations
